{
  "summary": "This change aborts FlushStateToDisk immediately if flushing block or undo data files fails. It stops the node from continuing to write block index metadata and coins cache entries to disk when the underlying block or undo data could not be made durable. The change also adds a test verifying that m_last_flushed_block is not advanced following a block file flush error.",
  "problem": "When FlushChainstateBlockFile fails, Bitcoin Core requests a shutdown but proceeds to flush block-index metadata and the UTXO set anyway, advancing m_last_flushed_block. This leaves on-disk state inconsistent, recording a block and its coins data as durable when the actual block or undo data may be missing or corrupt.",
  "evidence": [
    "Resolves a code TODO in validation.cpp originally deferred in PR #27866: 'Handle return error, or add detailed comment why it is safe to not return an error upon failure.'",
    "Description notes that advancing m_last_flushed_block on flush failure undermines invariants introduced in PR #34897, which intended to prevent persistent indexes from indexing ahead of durable chainstate."

result.summary: This change aborts FlushStateToDisk immediately if flushing block or undo data files fails. It stops the node from continuing to write block index metadata and coins cache entries to disk when the underlying block or undo data could not be made durable. The change also adds a test verifying that m_last_flushed_block is not advanced following a block file flush error.
result.problem: When FlushChainstateBlockFile fails, Bitcoin Core requests a shutdown but proceeds to flush block-index metadata and the UTXO set anyway, advancing m_last_flushed_block. This leaves on-disk state inconsistent, recording a block and its coins data as durable when the actual block or undo data may be missing or corrupt.
evidence: Resolves a code TODO in validation.cpp originally deferred in PR #27866: 'Handle return error, or add detailed comment why it is safe to not return an error upon failure.'

Description notes that advancing m_last_flushed_block on flush failure undermines invariants introduced in PR #34897, which intended to prevent persistent indexes from indexing ahead of durable chainstate.
result.scope_notes: Small and targeted change (+2/-3 in validation.cpp) accompanied by a unit test injecting an I/O failure.
result.card: Bitcoin Core aborts FlushStateToDisk early with an error if flushing block or undo data fails. Previously, a failure during block file flushing would request shutdown but still proceed to write block-index metadata and coins data, advancing the recorded flush position despite incomplete persistence. This prevented persistent indexes and state caches from maintaining proper durability invariants, risking inconsistent on-disk data. The change resolves a long-standing TODO from PR #27866 and ensures m_last_flushed_block remains at the last known successful flush point.
